title: Omit docstrings that only restate a private helper's name
answers: should I add a docstring to a small private helper
docstring restating function name review comment
does the repo want docstrings on private functions in scorer_utils
body:
Convention: a reviewer flagged a docstring that only restated the helper name as conflicting with the repository's Python guidance to omit redundant docstrings.
Where: mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py:_extract_params_from_signature was kept without a docstring; the descriptive name carries the meaning.
Fix pattern: For small private helpers, rely on a descriptive name and skip the docstring; add one only when it says something the name and code do not (e.g. non-obvious constraints).
Constraints: Public functions with real contracts, such as recreate_function, keep their docstrings describing arguments and behaviour.
applies: Private helpers in mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py and similar modules; reviewer-enforced, not a lint rule.
says: Pull request code reviews flag unnecessary comments that merely repeat internal function names.
Reviewers ask to remove redundant documentation from private helpers during code review.
search: Small private helpers such as _extract_params_from_signature in mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py should omit docstrings that only restate the function name. Descriptive function names carry the meaning, so docstrings should only be added when they convey non-obvious constraints not evident from the name and code. Public functions with formal contracts, such as recreate_function, must retain docstrings describing arguments and behavior. This convention is reviewer-enforced in scorer_utils.py and similar modules rather than checked by a lint rule.
